facts.fact: AIP states that the Citiweb software ONECI supplied to civil status centres is intended for the digital registration of births, marriages, deaths and other civil status acts.

AIP states that at the end of 2025 ONECI equipped all the civil status centres of the town halls and sub-prefectures with computer equipment carrying the Citiweb software; this is a statement of centres equipped, with no numerator or denominator given and no figure for centres registering with it.
AIP states that the civil status digitalisation reform is steered by ONECI, the national civil status and identification office, which supplied the centres with Citiweb.

The prefecture's secretary general acknowledged the European Union's financial support for the project supporting the digitalisation of civil status and the fight against documentary fraud; no domestic budget line is mentioned.
At the end of 2025 ONECI equipped all town hall and sub-prefecture civil status centres with computers carrying Citiweb, per AIP.

On 30 and 31 July 2026 the sub-prefects of the Gôh region were trained at Gagnoa on the new rules and the digital applications already deployed, after a first session on 27 to 29 July for civil status agents of the region's town halls and sub-prefectures.

systems.tiers: civil status centres of town halls (mairies) and sub-prefectures, all equipped at the end of 2025
